messages.text:
I agree with this plan, go ahead with the first step, ATLAS Pixel TDR and RD53A manual. 

Also suggest (if you can't create) a new local git branch and a PR description associated with it. Let's run this as a test case. Once read through we will go by (3.) of your plan focussing it.

I’ll start the pilot with the ATLAS Pixel TDR and RD53A manual: extract page-level text, check document identity and extraction quality, and build reusable document maps. I’ll keep the reading broad for now, ready for the focused engineering questions in step 3.

I’ll also try to create a local branch and prepare a PR description with the results and limitations.

The branch `m0/reference-reading-pilot` is created. I’m setting up a pinned PDF extractor in an ignored local environment, with text caches and page images kept out of Git.

CERN’s catalogue pages returned a bot challenge. I’ll use the downloaded title pages and accessible public indexes to check identity, and leave any unresolved metadata explicit.

The first extraction found two details worth preserving: the Pixel TDR file has a July 2018 cover despite its 2017 report number, and the RD53A manual is version 3.51, dated August 2019.

Text was extracted from 482 and 79 pages respectively. The Pixel TDR has bookmarks; RD53A has none, so its map will need the printed contents. I also found duplicated cover text and pages with no extracted text, which I’ll check visually.

The pilot caught a useful navigation problem: RD53A’s printed contents gives stale page numbers. For example, “Introduction” points to printed page 1, but starts on printed page 3, PDF page 4. I’ll build its map from the actual headings and footers.

The caches also preserve technical-table text, but the rendering checks show why we must inspect the original page before using table values or diagram labels.

The document maps are taking shape, and I’ve added ligature normalization so searches for words such as “flex” can find PDF text encoded as “ﬂex.”

Cache reuse is working in the initial timing checks. The guides will also flag RD53A’s prototype status and the Pixel TDR’s proposed designs, so the focused pass can distinguish those from production evidence.

The pilot checks now pass. Verified cache reuse took about 0.12 seconds for the Pixel TDR and 0.02 seconds for RD53A, compared with roughly 7 and 1 seconds for extraction on this machine. The four retrieval checks found the expected technical pages.

I’m finishing the guides, validation report, and PR description, then checking that PDFs and generated caches remain excluded from Git.

Completed the pilot on branch **`m0/reference-reading-pilot`**.

- Extracted all **561 pages** into reusable local caches.
- Added [document maps]([redacted] search/render tools, and verified identity metadata.
- Found and documented stale page references in RD53A’s contents.
- Prepared the [PR description]([redacted] and [validation report]([redacted]

**Checks:** 26 tests and four retrieval checks passed; all six session records validate. PDFs and caches remain ignored.

This covered extraction, broad mapping, and sampled reading—not a cover-to-cover scientific review. The material is ready for step 3’s focused questions.

ADR-005 remains DRAFT. No commits, pushes, or remote PR created.
